diagnosis.explanation: Design P017 (F003) shows strong visible absorption (G1=0.013) but suboptimal NIR reflectance (G2=0.407). Local derivatives indicate d2 (top Cr) and d4 (bottom Cr) have negative derivatives for G2 (-0.020 and -0.007 respectively), suggesting that decreasing these metal thicknesses could improve NIR reflectance by reducing parasitic absorption, while the derivative for G1 w.r.t d2 is also negative (-0.005), implying a potential tradeoff where thinning d2 might slightly reduce visible absorption. However, d1 (SiO2) has a missing G2 derivative, and d3 (HfO2) has a negative G2 derivative (-0.007) but is at its lower bound (50nm), preventing further decrease to test the hypothesis that thinner spacers improve NIR reflection in this specific stack configuration.

Design P028 (F001) achieves excellent NIR reflectance (G2=0.639) but suffers from higher visible reflectance (G1=0.094) compared to other candidates. Local derivatives show d1 (HfO2) and d3 (HfO2) have negative derivatives for G1 (-0.0076 and -0.0084), indicating that increasing these dielectric thicknesses improves visible absorption. However, d2 (Cr) has a positive G1 derivative (0.012), meaning increasing the top Cr layer worsens visible absorption. The current design is at the lower bounds for d1, d2, and d3. Refining the family bounds or exploring the interior of F001 with increased dielectric thicknesses is informative to balance the high G2 performance with improved G1, testing if the all-HfO2 spacer mechanism (R3) can be tuned for better visible coupling without sacrificing the achieved NIR reflection.

Design P009 (F001) presents a balanced profile (G1=0.041, G2=0.563). A local common ascent direction was identified involving decreasing d1 (HfO2), increasing d2 (Cr), and decreasing d3 (HfO2). The derivative data suggests d1 decrease improves both G1 and G2 locally. The action refines layers along this calculated joint direction to test the linearity of the response and potentially push G2 higher while maintaining low G1, exploiting the specific interference conditions of the HfO2/Cr/HfO2/Cr stack on Al.
